description: Polling staff need to keep track of voter assistance situations and accessibility accommodations throughout the day without losing procedural consistency or mixing up different exception cases. All locations are fictional.

user_profile.persona: 36-year-old deputy polling supervisor overseeing several front-desk interactions
user_profile.context: Most voters move through normally, but the special cases require enough precision that informal memory is not reliable
user_profile.communication_style: Respectful and exact, wants assistance cases logged without losing procedural detail

fact_sheet.fact: The Precinct Supervisor for the Maplewood Community Center is Eleanor Vance, reachable at the site phone on extension 401.
The designated IT Support Technician is Kenji Tanaka, and his direct cell number for urgent issues is (555) 821-4099.
Maria Flores is the assigned Spanish-language bilingual poll worker, stationed at the Greeter Desk (Station 1).
For procedural or legal questions, staff must contact the Redwood County Elections legal hotline at (555) 789-1234.
The polling place is located at Maplewood Community Center, 1250 Oak Street, Northwood, CA 94500.
Standard voter check-in is conducted at Stations 2 and 3 using the ePollster Tab 4 tablets.
The accessible voting machine, an OmniBallot 3000 model, is located at Station 5.
Curbside voting is conducted in two designated parking spots, C1 and C2, located near the west entrance.
A voter requesting curbside assistance must have Form C-19 completed by two poll workers of different party affiliations.
For language assistance other than Spanish, poll workers must use the LanguageLine phone service by dialing 1-800-555-LANG and providing account code 774-RW.
Any voter requiring assistance from another person to mark their ballot must have that person sign the 'Voter Assistance Declaration' in the poll roster.
A voter whose eligibility cannot be confirmed must be issued a provisional ballot using the pink P-04 envelope.
All voter assistance incidents must be logged in the 'PollWatch Sentinel' system.
The direct login URL for PollWatch Sentinel is https://redwood.pollwatch.gov/login.
The username for the Deputy Supervisor station (Station 4) is 'deputy_mcc' and the Election Day password is 'Maple!2024#'.
The Wi-Fi network for official polling equipment is 'RC_ELECTIONS_SECURE' and the password is 'VoteSafe24!'.
A full data sync for the ePollster tablets must be manually initiated at 12:00 PM and 5:00 PM to ensure roster accuracy.
A large-print ballot guide is available upon request; it is stored in the blue supply bin labeled 'ACC-LP' under Station 1.
The OmniBallot 3000 at Station 5 is equipped with an audio tactile interface (ATI) and a sip-and-puff device port.
A magnifying sheet for paper ballots is available at the Deputy Supervisor's station (Station 4).
All assistance animal incidents, such as a disruptive animal, must be logged in PollWatch Sentinel using incident code 'AA-02'.
In case of a power outage, the backup generator provides power to Stations 2, 3, 5, and the main ballot box light for exactly 4 hours.
If the PollWatch Sentinel system is offline, all incidents must be recorded manually on the 'Incident Log Form' (Form I-LOG-M) with exact timestamps.
If the OmniBallot 3000 machine malfunctions, the designated backup unit is stored in supply closet B, labeled 'Backup VB-02'.
The emergency evacuation meeting point for all poll workers is the large oak tree in the adjacent park, 300 feet east of the building exit.
If a voter has spoiled their ballot, they are entitled to a maximum of two replacement ballots, each logged in the roster.
The secure ballot box is located 10 feet from the main exit and is monitored by security Camera 4 on the precinct's CCTV system.
The end-of-day reconciliation must be co-signed by Eleanor Vance and the Deputy Supervisor on Form EOD-7 before sealing any materials.

user_needs.description: What are the login URL, username, and password for the PollWatch Sentinel system at my station?
What is the procedure if the PollWatch Sentinel system is offline?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After a user asks how to log into a critical system, a natural follow-up is to provide the contingency plan for when that system is unavailable.

user_needs.description: A voter needs language assistance in a language other than Spanish. What is the procedure and what information do I need?
Who is our assigned Spanish-language poll worker and where are they located?
user_needs.prediction_reason: INTRA-GROUP: After asking about the general procedure for language assistance, the user will likely want to know about the specific, in-person resource for the most common language.

user_needs.description: For curbside assistance, what form must be completed and by how many poll workers of different party affiliations?
Where are the designated parking spots for curbside voting located?
user_needs.prediction_reason: INTRA-GROUP: Once the user knows the procedure for curbside voting, they will need to know the physical location to direct staff and voters.

user_needs.description: A voter has requested a large-print ballot guide. Where is it stored?
Where can I find the magnifying sheet for voters who need help reading a paper ballot?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After a user asks about one specific type of visual aid (large-print guide), it is helpful to proactively offer information about other available visual aids like the magnifying sheet.

user_needs.description: Where is the OmniBallot 3000 accessible voting machine located?
What specific accessibility features are available on the OmniBallot 3000?
user_needs.prediction_reason: INTRA-GROUP: After locating the accessible voting machine, the user may need to describe its specific capabilities to a voter.

user_needs.description: If the OmniBallot 3000 machine malfunctions, where is the designated backup unit stored?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: Knowing the location of the primary accessible machine naturally leads to a concern about what to do if it fails.

user_needs.description: Who is the IT Support Technician and what is their direct number for urgent issues?
user_needs.prediction_reason: INTRA-GROUP: After learning about a hardware failure contingency (backup unit), the user will need the contact information for the person who can fix the primary unit or assist with the backup.

user_needs.description: What is the correct procedure for a voter whose eligibility cannot be confirmed in the ePollster?

user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After handling a legally sensitive situation like a provisional ballot, the user might want to know the contact for official legal guidance for future issues.
